No new health zone was affected this cycle; the roster holds at 46 zones across five provinces. SitRep64 publishes per-zone DAY columns rather than a full cumulative table, so cumulatives are the promoted SitRep63 basis plus this cycle's deltas: Ituri Bunia +25, Mongbwalu +8, Nizi +9, Mangala +1, Lita +10, Nia-Nia +5, Bambu +5, Tchomia +2, Kilo +1, Mambasa +3, Fataki +3, Aru +1, Ariwara +2 (= the stated +75); Nord-Kivu Katwa +5, Butembo +2 (= +7); Haut-Uele Wamba +4 (= +4). Death deltas: Ituri Bunia +4, Rwampara +3, Mongbwalu +3, Nizi +4, Nyankunde +1, Mangala +1, Lita +1, Nia-Nia +2, Bambu +1, Tchomia +1, Kilo +1, Logo +1, Mambasa +1, Fataki +1 (= the stated +25); Nord-Kivu Katwa +4 (= +4). Rwampara and Nyankunde recorded deaths with no new cases, and Logo recorded its first confirmed death. Sud-Kivu and Tshopo recorded no movement. Haut-Uele's province row is footnoted by INSP as under revision for harmonization/reclassification, so its 22/13 is carried as printed and no trend is fitted to it. The Ituri unventilated residual holds at 17 and keeps its established internal row label 'Autres ZS (donnees non ventilees)' so the non-zone aggregate stays a residual.

reconciliation.note: Named health-zone rows sum to 2250 confirmed / 893 confirmed deaths across all five provinces. Table 1 province totals: Ituri 2023/745, Nord-Kivu 214/130, Sud-Kivu 3/1, Haut-Uele 22/13, Tshopo 5/4 = national 2267/893, and the province rows sum exactly to the national totals this cycle (no residual). The Ituri named rows (2006) plus the 17 explicitly unventilated cases reconcile to the 1948+75 = 2023 province total; the unventilated block is unchanged at 17 and is never smeared across named zones. The single DRC unallocated residual is therefore that 17-case Ituri block (country-scope 37 with the 20 Uganda anchor). The national cumulative is additive from SitRep63: 2181 + 86 = 2267 cases and 864 + 29 = 893 deaths, with no retrospective consolidation this cycle. SitRep64 prints per-zone DAY columns rather than a full cumulative zone table, so each zone cumulative is the promoted SitRep63 basis plus its SitRep64 delta; the deltas sum exactly to the stated +75 Ituri / +7 Nord-Kivu / +4 Haut-Uele cases and +25 Ituri / +4 Nord-Kivu deaths. Carrying the promoted SitRep63 Katwa basis (62, not the printed 63) forward by its +4 gives 66 and holds Nord-Kivu's named death sum at the province total 130, so the SitRep63 over-count no longer leaves a residual. Miti-Murhesa (Sud-Kivu) reached 52 consecutive days with no new confirmed case and stays in residual surveillance, so 46 zones are touched and 45 are actively transmitting.

lab_indicators_24h.note: National aggregate: Ituri 211 samples documented in the collection network / 75 positive (61 living, 14 deaths) = 35.5%; Nord-Kivu 119 analyzed / 8 positive = 6.7%. Positivity uses 83 positives over 330 analyzed samples (Ituri + Nord-Kivu). Haut-Uele contributed 4 new positives from the Nia-Nia laboratory (its 4 collected samples await shipment and are excluded from the analyzed denominator). Sud-Kivu and Tshopo report no laboratory line this cycle and are excluded rather than carried forward at their SitRep63 values. Ituri's apparent positivity nearly doubled (18.6% -> 35.5%) on a smaller documented denominator (236 -> 211), which is a test-targeting shift, not a measured prevalence change. The day's laboratory positives (75 + 8 + 4 = 87) exceed the promoted +86 confirmations by one at Nord-Kivu (8 positives against +7 confirmed); see preserved_conflicts.

care_continuity: SitRep64 Tableau 6: 722 in isolation at end of day at 85.9% global bed occupancy (722/841 beds); Ituri 78.0% (548/700), Nord-Kivu 123.4% (174/141) on a capacity reported again this cycle after being absent on 16/07. Haut-Uele and Tshopo report ND, so Tshopo leaves the occupancy table rather than being carried at a stale rate. The bed identity closes exactly at every level (721 J-1 + 119 admissions - 118 exits = 722; Ituri 542 + 86 - 80 = 548; Nord-Kivu 179 + 33 - 38 = 174). Exits over 24h (118 total): 19 deaths, 56 non-cases, 32 recoveries, 11 escapes. The confirmed/suspect split is the one part that does not close (252 + 460 = 712 against the 722 census, and Nord-Kivu 17 + 155 = 172 against its own 174); the census is promoted and the residual carried on suspects at 470. Ituri first-line personnel: 119 cumulative infections, 61 recovered, 22 hospitalized, 36 deaths (CFR 30.3%), with no new infection reported on 17/07.

Recovered did NOT advance and the promoted figure is known to be stale: the cover repeats 412 while also printing +32 daily Ituri recoveries, and the narrative's Ituri cumulative of 406 reconciles exactly with SitRep63's promoted Ituri component (374 + 32). Reconstructing from components gives a national 443 (Ituri 406 + Nord-Kivu 36 + Tshopo 1), a figure the source never prints, so the cover's 412 is carried unchanged and country-scope recovered holds at 423. Treat the recovered series as stalled and under-stated pending INSP reconciliation.
highlights: 86 new confirmed cases (Ituri 75, Nord-Kivu 7, Haut-Uele 4) and 29 new deaths (Ituri 25, Nord-Kivu 4); DRC cumulative 2267 confirmed / 893 deaths (CFR 39.4%). New confirmations rose sharply from 56 to 86, the largest single-cycle case count of the outbreak so far, while Ituri's alert-investigation rate continued recovering to 90.9% from 68.9% and 28.1% two cycles ago. The case rise tracks the third consecutive cycle of widening detection capacity, so it measures how much of the outbreak is being seen rather than establishing re-acceleration.

Contact follow-up rose to 83.64% nationally (9886/11820) from 66.9%, but the population under follow-up fell by 1751 in a single cycle with no explanation in the source. The coverage gain is a joint numerator-and-denominator movement and is not read as a transmission improvement. Ituri reached 83.0% (7192/8660) and Nord-Kivu 87.0% (2618/3008); Haut-Uele reports no rate at all, and the province rows sum exactly to the national totals for the first time in several cycles.

No new health zone was affected: the roster holds at 46 touched and 45 actively transmitting, with Miti-Murhesa (Sud-Kivu) at day 52 without a confirmed case. Ituri's rise is broad rather than focal, with 13 zones adding cases and Bunia alone adding 25 to reach 606, while Rwampara and Nyankunde recorded deaths without new cases and Logo recorded its first confirmed death. The Uganda-border axis stayed active (Ariwara +2, Aru +1, Mahagi holding at 1), and Haut-Uele added 4 more Wamba cases under an explicit INSP revision footnote.

alerts_total.data_gap_note: Tableau 3 (at 17/07): 1227 alerts of the day across Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Haut-Uele and Tshopo (Sud-Kivu reports ND). Investigated 93.6% (1148/1227): Ituri 90.9% (402/442), Nord-Kivu 99.5% (741/745), Haut-Uele 10.3% (4/39), Tshopo 100.0% (1/1). Every column reconciles exactly this cycle: the Report-J-1 / new-alert split closes (44 + 1183 = 1227) where it failed to at SitRep63, and the province rows sum exactly to the national totals for alerts (1227), investigated (1148), validated-living (147 = 112+31+3+1), validated-deceased (89 = 58+30+1+0) and suspects (236). Validated suspects 236 = 147 living + 89 community deaths under investigation. Ituri's investigation rate completed a three-cycle recovery to 90.9% from 68.9% and 28.1%, leaving 40 alerts uninvestigated against 121 last cycle. Haut-Uele reported 39 alerts with only 4 investigated (10.3%), its weakest rate of the outbreak, in its first alert column after the backfill cycle.

challenges.finding: Reticence toward post-mortem sampling (EDS/swabs), community resistance and insecurity targeting EDS teams (attack at the Muchanga bridge; activities paralysed at Nyankunde) delay confirmation and under-estimate cases.
challenges.response: Intensify CREC/RCCE, involve religious and community leaders, secure teams, and increase the number of EDS teams.

challenges.finding: Non-payment of frontline providers (strike in the Bunia and Rwampara health zones; return to work announced after the Ituri military governor's intervention) interrupts response activities including dignified and secure burials.
challenges.response: Regularize provider payment and secure dedicated financing.

challenges.finding: Insufficient CTE/CT capacity, driving admission delays and nosocomial transmission risk. The row prints 126.2% Nord-Kivu occupancy on a carried 15/07 denominator and 78% in Ituri (541 patients for 693 beds) with 51 severe or critical patients; the SitRep64 tables give Nord-Kivu 123.4% (174/141, capacity reported again) and Ituri 78.0% (548/700). SOURCE NOTE: this row prints SitRep63 figures and is carried forward stale; the SitRep64 tables supersede it.
challenges.response: Accelerate CTE construction and expansion, deploy temporary structures, and report bed capacity systematically.

challenges.finding: Contact follow-up performance in sharp decline, leaving transmission chains uninterrupted. The row prints Ituri 61.5% against 78.1% on 15/07, Haut-Uele 54.0%, Tshopo 72.0% and national 66.9%; the SitRep64 Tableau 4 gives national 83.64% (9886/11820), Ituri 83.0%, Nord-Kivu 87.0% and Tshopo 50.0%, on a denominator that fell by 1751. SOURCE NOTE: this row prints SitRep63 figures and is carried forward stale; the SitRep64 tables supersede it.
challenges.response: Train, deploy and motivate community relays (RECO) with reinforced supervision, and investigate the drop observed in Ituri.

challenges.finding: Insufficient ambulances and weak prepositioning at points of control, causing transfer and isolation delays.
challenges.response: Preposition ambulances including at PoE/PoC, and deploy transit centres by health zone.

challenges.finding: Insufficient supply of essential medicines (MEG) and medical inputs, weakening overall case management.
challenges.response: Advocacy and urgent procurement of essential medicines.

challenges.finding: Insufficient IPC inputs (PPE, chlorine) and limited functional triage units (175 of 1170, 15%), carrying a high nosocomial-infection risk against 119 cumulative first-line personnel infections including 36 deaths.
challenges.response: Urgent procurement and reinforced IPC training.

challenges.finding: Geographic extension (Haut-Uele, Tshopo) combined with high mobility, carrying urban, riverine and cross-border diffusion risk.
challenges.response: Activate the 23 priority Haut-Uele PoE/PoC and reinforce cross-border coordination.

challenges.finding: Proximity laboratories at Butembo, Mambasa and Logo are still being installed, leaving long confirmation delays and undetected transmission.
challenges.response: Accelerate deployment of decentralized diagnostic capacity.

challenges.finding: Insufficient financial resources limit implementation across the response pillars.
challenges.response: Urgent resource mobilization and advocacy with partners.

challenges.finding: Insecurity and limited access (CODECO, ADF) restrict operations.
challenges.response: Reinforce security coordination and humanitarian access.

challenges.finding: Continuity of essential health services (CEHS) is compromised, raising indirect non-Ebola mortality.
challenges.response: Effective implementation of free care and reinforcement of CEHS.

contacts_total.data_gap_note: Tableau 4 (17 July): 11820 under follow-up, 9886 seen, 83.64% national (displayed 83.6%), up from 66.9%. Province rows: Ituri 83.0% (7192/8660), Nord-Kivu 87.0% (2618/3008), Tshopo 50.0% (76/152); Haut-Uele reports ND. Unlike SitRep63, the province rows sum EXACTLY to the national totals this cycle (8660+3008+152 = 11820 under follow-up; 7192+2618+76 = 9886 seen), and the cover KPI and Table 4 agree, so no rate cluster is in conflict. The national denominator fell materially from 13571 to 11820 (-1751) without explanation in the source; the rate rise is therefore partly a denominator effect and must not be read as a transmission improvement. Tshopo's 50.0% (76/152) is byte-identical to SitRep63 and is likely carried forward rather than re-measured.

patient_movement_total.data_gap_note: SitRep64 Tableau 6 end-of-day census 722 at 85.9% occupancy (722/841 beds): Ituri 548 @78.0% (700 beds, 86 admissions, 80 exits), Nord-Kivu 174 @123.4% (141 beds, 33 admissions, 38 exits). Haut-Uele and Tshopo report ND, so Tshopo drops out of the occupancy table rather than being carried at its stale 16/07 rate. The bed identity CLOSES exactly at every level this cycle: Ituri 542 + 86 - 80 = 548, Nord-Kivu 179 + 33 - 38 = 174, national 721 + 119 - 118 = 722. Exits over 24h (118 total): 19 deaths, 56 non-cases, 32 recoveries, 11 escapes, 0 HGR transfers. Nord-Kivu reported a bed capacity again this cycle (141) after its absence on 16/07, so its 123.4% is measured rather than computed on a carried denominator. The printed J-1 census (721) is one below SitRep63's printed end-of-day census (722), a cross-cycle discontinuity in the source rather than an intra-document identity failure. The confirmed/suspect split does not close against the census (252 + 460 = 712 vs 722) and is resolved on the suspect side; see preserved_conflicts.

poe_poc_combined_ituri_nord_kivu.scope_note: SitRep64 reports PoE/PoC as a combined Ituri + Nord-Kivu block (75 points: Ituri 60, Nord-Kivu 15) rather than the Ituri-only block of prior cycles, so it is carried under a combined key and NOT under poe_poc_ituri; no Ituri-only split is published and none is inferred. One dead body was intercepted in Nord-Kivu.

priorities.priority: Explain the 13571 -> 11820 contact-denominator drop before reading the 66.9% -> 83.6% coverage rise as progress, and lift Haut-Uele's 10.3% alert-investigation rate (4 of 39) while holding Ituri's recovery to 90.9%.

Relieve Nord-Kivu isolation saturation at 123.4% (174 of 141 beds) and reconcile the Tableau-6 confirmed/suspect split, which falls 10 short of the 722 census nationally and 2 short of the 174 census in Nord-Kivu.

Keep the Uganda-border axis in view: Ariwara added 2 confirmations and Aru 1, with Mahagi holding at 1; sustain PoE/PoC screening across the 75 combined Ituri + Nord-Kivu points that registered 167229 travellers.

Resolve the 17 unventilated Ituri confirmed cases without smearing them across named zones, and reconcile the zone-table total row (which prints +56 new cases against the +86 carried everywhere else in the document).
Sustain residual epidemiological surveillance in Sud-Kivu, where Miti-Murhesa has reached 52 consecutive days with no new confirmed case, toward a provincial end-of-outbreak declaration.

preserved_conflicts: SitRep64 national headline is DRC-only (2267 confirmed / 893 confirmed deaths across five provinces); the country-scope snapshot adds the Uganda component (20/2/11) separately -> 2287 confirmed / 895 deaths / 423 recovered.

The detailed zone table's total row is partially stale. It prints 'Nouv. cas' = 56 and a community/intra-CTE death split of 18 + 18 = 36, which are SitRep63's values, while its cumulative cells (2267 / 893 / 39.40%) and its new-death cell (29) are current. The cover KPI, the Table 1 province row totals, the section-1 narrative and the summed per-zone day columns all give +86 (Ituri 75, Nord-Kivu 7, Haut-Uele 4), and only +86 closes 2181 + 86 = 2267, so +86 is promoted. The current cycle's own death split is Ituri 14 community + 11 intra-CTE = 25 plus Nord-Kivu 4, per the section-1 narrative.

The zone table's death subcolumns carry SitRep63's 18 + 18 community/intra-CTE split on the total row against this cycle's +29. The province table and the section-1 narrative agree on +29 (Ituri 25, of which 14 community and 11 intra-CTE; Nord-Kivu 4) and the per-zone death deltas sum exactly to 25 and 4 respectively, so the province/narrative split is promoted and the stale subcolumns are not reconciled.

Recovered is NOT advanced this cycle and the promoted 412 is known to be stale. The cover prints 412 cumulative, byte-identical to SitRep63, alongside '+32 gueris (Ituri 32)'; the section-1 narrative states Ituri's cumulative recovered 'portant le cumul des gueris a 406', which reconciles EXACTLY with SitRep63's promoted Ituri component (374 + 32 = 406) and therefore shows the cover's 412 is a carry-forward that failed to advance rather than a competing measurement. Reconstructing the national from its components gives Ituri 406 + Nord-Kivu 36 (unchanged, 0 recovery exits) + Tshopo 1 = 443; SitRep64 also states Tshopo holds '1 gueri' against SitRep63's promoted 2, so the component basis itself moved. Because 443 is a figure the source never prints and the recovered series feeds public deliverables, the printed cover value 412 is promoted unchanged and the reconstruction is preserved here rather than published as a headline. Country-scope recovered therefore also holds flat at 423. Treat the recovered series as stalled and under-stated pending INSP reconciliation, NOT as evidence that no one recovered.

The national contact denominator fell from 13571 to 11820 (-1751) in one cycle with no explanation in the source, while contacts seen rose from 9079 to 9886. The 66.9% -> 83.64% coverage rise is therefore a joint numerator-and-denominator movement; the source does not distinguish completed follow-up from delisting or reclassification, so no transmission inference is drawn from it. Unlike SitRep63 the province rows sum exactly to the national totals and no rate cluster conflicts.

Tableau 6's isolation split does not close against its own census: the narrative states 722 in isolation 'dont 252 cas confirmes et 460 cas suspects', which sums to 712, a gap of 10. The same failure recurs one level down: Nord-Kivu's narrative gives '174 malades ... (17 confirmes, 155 suspects)', which sums to 172 against its own printed 174. The 722 census is triple-corroborated (85.9% occupancy over 841 beds; the province columns 548 + 174 = 722; and the bed identity 721 + 119 - 118 = 722, which closes exactly) and is promoted. Following the SitRep63 Katwa precedent of promoting the corroborated total and carrying the residual on the single unreliable component, the suspect count is carried at 470 to hold the census and the printed 460 is preserved here. The direction of that adjustment is a REVIEW JUDGMENT, not a source value: suspects are the churn-heavy category (56 non-case exits this cycle alone) while confirmed-in-isolation is a tracked roster, so the residual is placed on suspects. If INSP later reconciles the split the other way, the confirmed figure moves to 262 and the suspect figure returns to 460.

The bed identity CLOSES exactly at every level this cycle (Ituri 542 + 86 - 80 = 548; Nord-Kivu 179 + 33 - 38 = 174; national 721 + 119 - 118 = 722), unlike SitRep63 where the Nord-Kivu column was off by one. What does not close is across cycles: SitRep64's printed J-1 census (721) sits one below SitRep63's printed end-of-day census (722). The SitRep64 J-1 value is used for the identity because it is the basis the document's own arithmetic runs on; the discontinuity is recorded here rather than reconciled.

The day's laboratory positives exceed the day's confirmations by one: Ituri 75 positives against +75 confirmed and Haut-Uele 4 against +4 reconcile exactly, but Nord-Kivu records 8 positives against only +7 confirmed cases (75 + 8 + 4 = 87 vs the promoted +86). The +86 case figure is promoted; the extra Nord-Kivu positive is preserved as an unreconciled laboratory-to-case-registration lag.

Haut-Uele's province row (22 confirmed / 13 deaths) is explicitly footnoted by INSP as under revision for harmonization and reclassification. It is carried as printed and its +4 Wamba cases are promoted, but no trend, rate or delta is fitted to Haut-Uele this cycle; its 39 alerts with 4 investigated and its absent contact-follow-up rate inherit the same caution. This follows the SitRep63 backfill cycle, so two consecutive cycles of Haut-Uele figures are provisional.

The cover death footnote is truncated mid-sentence ('Letalite globale 39,4% (893 / 2 267) :.'), so the customary 864 + 29 = 893 arithmetic line is absent. The arithmetic is nonetheless exact and 893/2267 = 39.4% matches the printed CFR, so the headline is promoted without it.

The SitRep64 challenge table is partially carried forward and cites contact-follow-up and CTE-occupancy figures from earlier reporting days that disagree with the SitRep64 operational tables. The tables are promoted for every numeric indicator; the challenge rows are retained only for their qualitative findings and responses.

Tshopo's contact line (76 seen / 152 under follow-up / 50.0%) is byte-identical to SitRep63 and is carried as printed; it is likely a carried-forward row rather than a re-measurement, and Tshopo also drops out of the Tableau-6 occupancy table entirely this cycle rather than being carried at its stale 25.0% rate.

46 health zones are affected but only 45 carry active transmission. Miti-Murhesa (Sud-Kivu) reached its 52nd consecutive day with no new confirmed case and remains outside the active set in residual surveillance. Both counts are carried and are not interchangeable.

The cover per-province CFR line (Ituri 36.8%, Nord-Kivu 60.7%, Haut-Uele 59.1%, Sud-Kivu 33.3%, Tshopo 80.0%) agrees with Table 1 for all five provinces (745/2023 = 36.8%; 130/214 = 60.7%; 13/22 = 59.1%; 1/3 = 33.3%; 4/5 = 80.0%). review_notes: SitRep #064 (report date 2026-07-17; cover publication 2026-07-18; INSP post 25159; media 25160; WP publish 2026-07-18T23:28:36Z). PDF sha256 9458cd2adaea90b7bd8002c4c6d869b34d615e05eab3e224a69fa06f31f49a53, 13 pages, 5002431 bytes, byte-verified against the live INSP upload and the source-librarian visual receipt (all 13 pages rendered; contact sheet plus pages 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 inspected).

DRC 2267 confirmed / 893 deaths / CFR 39.4% / 412 recovered (stale, see conflicts: the component reconstruction gives 443); +86 confirmed / +29 deaths in 24h (Ituri 75/25, Nord-Kivu 7/4, Haut-Uele 4/0; Sud-Kivu and Tshopo zero). Isolation census 722 at 85.9% occupancy over 841 beds, with the bed identity closing exactly at every level; the confirmed/suspect split does not close and the residual is carried on suspects (252/470 against a printed 252/460). Contact follow-up 83.64% (9886/11820), up from 66.9% on a denominator that fell by 1751. Five provinces; 46 health zones touched and 45 with active transmission.

No new health zone this cycle (roster holds at 46). Per-zone cumulatives are the promoted SitRep63 basis plus SitRep64 day-column deltas, which sum exactly to the stated province increments; carrying the promoted Katwa 62 forward by +4 holds Nord-Kivu's named death sum at the province total 130, closing the SitRep63 over-count with no residual. Province rows sum exactly to the national totals for cases, deaths, alerts and contacts this cycle. The Uganda-border axis stayed active (Ariwara +2, Aru +1, Mahagi holding at 1).

Country-scope adds Uganda (20/2/11) -> 2287 confirmed / 895 deaths / 423 recovered. Country-scope unallocated is 37 (17 Ituri unventilated + 20 Uganda). Source-internal conflicts resolved to the internally-consistent values and preserved in preserved_conflicts: the zone-table total row printing +56 new cases against +86 everywhere else (a stale SitRep63 carry-over); the zone-table death subcolumn total not summing; recovered frozen at 412 while +32 daily and an Ituri cumulative of 406 are also printed, the latter reconciling exactly with SitRep63's Ituri component and implying a national 443; the unexplained -1751 contact-denominator drop; Tableau 6's 252+460 = 712 split against its own 722 census (and Nord-Kivu's 17+155 = 172 against 174), resolved on the suspect side; the zone-table total row carrying stale SitRep63 new-case and death-split cells; Nord-Kivu's 8 laboratory positives against +7 confirmed; and Haut-Uele's row flagged by INSP as under revision. The challenge table is partially carried forward and is used qualitatively only.

Source-review correction: the upstream review packet summarised Tableau 6's J-1 census as 722 (the document prints 721, and the bed identity closes exactly on 721), reported the bed identity as off by one, gave Ituri's investigation rate as 91.0% (the document prints 90,9 %), and stated that the per-province validated living/deceased alert split was not published (Tableau 3 publishes it: Ituri 112/58, Nord-Kivu 31/30, Haut-Uele 3/1, Tshopo 1/0, summing exactly to 147/89). All four were corrected against the archived PDF bytes (sha256 9458cd2a...) before promotion, and the Tableau-3 Report-J-1/new-alert split was verified to reconcile this cycle (44 + 1183 = 1227) where it did not at SitRep63.
